Chapter 3: Understanding Motivations—What Drives Each Stakeholder
Now that we’ve mapped out the key players, the next step is figuring out what really makes each one tick. In complex sales, every stakeholder walks in with their own priorities, their own worries, and their own expectations.
If you can see the world through their eyes, you’re not just another salesperson—you’re a true strategist.
Let’s break down what motivates each buying influence.
First, you’ve got the Economic Buyer. These folks are all about the big picture. They want to know, "How will this purchase impact our bottom line?" Maybe it’ll save money, boost revenue, or help reduce risk. So naturally, their questions circle around cost, return on investment, and whether your solution fits the company’s long-term strategy.
Next, there’s the User Buyer. For them, it’s all about their day-to-day experience. Will this make their job easier, or is it going to throw a wrench into the routine? Are they going to need new skills? Their concerns are immediate and practical—real, hands-on stuff.
Then we have the Technical Buyer. Think of them as the gatekeepers for standards and policies. They want to know, "Is this safe? Is it compliant? Will it play nicely with what we already have?" Their questions dig into specs, integration, and risk management.
And finally, there’s the Coach. These are your champions inside the organization. They’re driven by relationships and a desire to see the project win. Sometimes, they’re hoping the success of your solution lines up with their own goals, or maybe even gives their reputation a little boost.
Now, here’s something to really pay attention to: uncovering these motivations isn’t just about asking the right questions. It’s about listening—really listening—with empathy, and picking up on what’s not being said. Sometimes, those unspoken cues matter just as much as the ones out in the open.
I like to think of each stakeholder as a traveler on their own journey. Every one of them is heading somewhere different, and your job is to show them how your solution helps them reach their destination.
For the Economic Buyer, that might be financial security. For the User Buyer, it’s a smoother workflow. The Technical Buyer? Peace of mind. And the Coach is looking for a win they can call their own.
So, how do you really get to the heart of what drives each person? Here are a few steps that help:
Spend time with each stakeholder one-on-one, if you can. Ask about their goals, their biggest headaches, and what they’re hoping to achieve. Listen closely for what lights them up—and what keeps them up at night. And pay attention to how they interact with others around them.
When you truly understand what matters to each person, you can tailor your message and your solution so it really hits home. That not only makes a sale more likely, but it builds real trust—and sets up a partnership that lasts.
Let’s bring this to life with a real-world example. Imagine you’re selling into a healthcare organization. The Economic Buyer is focused on cutting costs. The User Buyer—a nurse manager—is worried about patient safety. The Technical Buyer, maybe the IT director, wants airtight data privacy. And your Coach, a department head, is hoping to be seen as an innovator.
When you address each of their concerns directly—showing how your solution meets financial, practical, technical, and personal needs—you create true alignment. And that’s when you move from just making a sale, to building a real partnership.
